cameraDirections:
Main Line: Downstream from cleanout
Branch: Kitchen lateral

defects.title: No Defect — Cleanout Access & Pipe Material Identification
defects.narrative: At approximately 12 seconds / 4 feet, the cleanout was successfully accessed at the rear of the property. Pipe material identified as 3" ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene). No visible defects, blockages, or obstructions present. Clear flow observed with proper hydraulic grade. This establishes a baseline condition for the system at the point of entry.

defects.title: No Defect — Clear Transition Joint
defects.narrative: At approximately 38 seconds / 16 feet, a standard transition joint between ABS and Cast Iron sections was observed. Joint is properly aligned with no displacement, gaps, or leakage. Smooth transition with no lip or obstruction. Flow direction confirmed as downstream from cleanout toward municipal main.

defects.title: Light Tuberculation — Cast Iron Surface Oxidation
defects.narrative: At approximately 28 seconds / 11 feet, light tuberculation and surface oxidation were observed on the cast iron pipe walls. Approximately 15-20% reduction in interior diameter due to scale buildup. Flow remains unobstructed but surface friction has increased. This is typical age-related wear for cast iron systems and should be monitored during future inspections.

defects.title: Fine Hairline Root Intrusion — Early Stage
defects.narrative: At approximately 1 minute 3 seconds / 27 feet, fine hairline root intrusion was observed entering through the bell joint. Roots measure less than 1mm in diameter with no massing or obstruction present. No visible joint displacement or cracking. This represents early-stage root infiltration common in properties with mature landscaping. Immediate repair not required, but monitoring and possible preventive treatment recommended.

defects.title: Offset Joint — Physical Lip with Debris Accumulation
defects.narrative: At approximately 1 minute 42 seconds / 41 feet, a measurable offset joint was identified creating a physical lip on the invert. Vertical displacement measures approximately 1/4 inch. Debris accumulation noted at the lip, creating a catch point for solids. This condition reduces hydraulic efficiency and increases the likelihood of future blockages. Professional evaluation and scheduled repair or lining recommended.

defects.title: Pipe Sag — Standing Water with Sediment Accumulation
defects.narrative: At approximately 2 minutes 18 seconds / 56 feet, a pronounced belly (sag) was observed spanning approximately 6 linear feet. Standing water present at 1/4 inch depth with visible sediment settling along the invert. This low point creates a trap for debris and solids, potentially leading to blockage over time. While flow is currently maintained, this condition is likely to worsen as sediment continues to accumulate.

defects.title: Moderate Root Mass — Partial Obstruction
defects.narrative: At approximately 2 minutes 35 seconds / 64 feet, a moderate root mass was observed occupying approximately 35-40% of the pipe diameter. Multiple roots have entered through a joint, trapping debris and creating a partial obstruction. Reduced flow capacity noted at this location. Professional root cutting and chemical treatment recommended to restore proper flow.

defects.title: Severe Root Mass Obstruction — Critical Blockage
defects.narrative: At approximately 2 minutes 55 seconds / 72 feet, a severe root mass obstruction was identified. The root mass occupies approximately 65-70% of the pipe diameter with multiple large roots entering through a compromised joint. Significant debris and sediment trapped behind the root mass. Flow is severely restricted, creating a high risk of complete blockage and potential sewage backup. The pipe joint has been displaced by root growth pressure. Immediate professional intervention required.

defects.title: Longitudinal Fracture — Structural Failure with Soil Intrusion
defects.narrative: At approximately 3 minutes 34 seconds / 89 feet, a longitudinal fracture was identified in the pipe body. The crack spans approximately 18 inches in length and measures 3/8 inch in width. Visible soil intrusion confirms the pipe wall has completely failed. This condition compromises structural integrity and poses an immediate risk of collapse or soil erosion beneath the property. Urgent excavation and pipe replacement required.

defects.title: Heavy Grease and FOG Accumulation — Reduced Flow Capacity
defects.narrative: At approximately 4 minutes 5 seconds / 104 feet, heavy grease and FOG (Fats, Oils, Grease) accumulation was identified throughout the pipe walls. The buildup reduces the pipe's effective diameter by approximately 40-50%, creating a sticky surface that traps debris. Strong odor detected at this location. Regular hydro-jetting maintenance is needed to prevent complete blockage and restore flow capacity.

recommendations: Immediate excavation and pipe replacement required at the 61 ft fracture within 48 hours.
Schedule professional hydro-jetting within 30–60 days to clear FOG buildup.
Re-inspect root intrusion at 12 ft in 12 months.

statementOfServiceExtraSections.heading: Narratives
statementOfServiceExtraSections.body: The inspector observed normal wear patterns consistent with the age of the structure. The system performed within expected parameters given the pipe material and installation date. Property owner should maintain annual inspection intervals to track progression of noted conditions.

scopeText: A sewer inspection scan was requested of the main drain line from the structure to the city, private sewer connection, 150 feet or camera limitations (whichever comes first). The sewer line is to be accessed through a cleanout, roof vent (single story only) or other access point(s) to be determined best by the inspector. The camera inspection does not inspect all of the drain lines running under and or within the structure. The following is a summative report of the findings. If a video was completed, it will be posted on You Tube with the URL provided to promote understanding and transparency with our clients.
pointOfReference: This inspection evaluates the main sewer lateral from the structure to the municipal main or private sewer connection, up to a maximum distance of 150 feet or the physical limitations of the camera equipment (whichever comes first). The sewer line is accessed via an exterior cleanout, a single-story roof vent, or another access point deemed safest and most effective by the inspector. This inspection is strictly limited to the primary main line and does not evaluate secondary drain lines running beneath or within the interior structure. The following is a summary of our findings. If a video recording was completed, it will be uploaded to YouTube with the private URL link provided below to ensure full transparency and understanding.
statementOfService:
LV Sewer Inspections was retained for a survey of the listed structure's main sewer line in an effort to identify any areas of suspect blockages, deficiencies or damage and to document the areas for further review and or action by associated trades professional. Further investigations into these areas or destructive testing may reveal additional conditions that were not readily visible at the time of inspection. This report is based on information obtained at the site at the given date and time of the inspection.

This report is for the exclusive use of our client and is not intended for any other purpose. The report is based on the information available to us at the time as described in the report. Should additional information become available at a later date, we reserve the right to determine the impact, if any, the new information may have on our discovery and recommendations and to revise our opinions and conclusions if necessary and warranted.

We recommend all areas we locate in this report showing anomalies should be evaluated further to find out the cause and be repaired. Our recommendations are not intended as criticisms of the structure, but rather as professional opinions regarding conditions that we observed at the time of our inspection.
sevNoneDef: No actionable deficiencies were observed at the time of inspection. This classification documents the system's baseline attributes—such as pipe material (e.g., PVC, Cast Iron, ABS), flow direction, and general configuration. It establishes a structural and operational benchmark for future maintenance or comparative assessments.
sevNoneEg: Field Examples: Standard joint alignments, unobstructed flow, smooth transitions, or the identification and location of an accessible cleanout.
sevMinorDef: An incidental finding that does not currently restrict hydraulic flow or compromise the structural integrity of the pipe. These are typically early-stage wear characteristics or minor settling anomalies. Immediate repair is not required, but these areas should be documented and monitored during routine future inspections to track potential progression.
sevMinorEg: Field Examples: Light tuberculation or scale buildup in cast iron, fine "hairline" root intrusion at a joint without massing, slight surface pitting, or minor cosmetic scoring.
sevModDef: A functional or structural impairment that hinders the optimal performance of the waste line. While the system may currently be draining, these issues create high-risk "catch points" for debris, accelerating solids accumulation and escalating the probability of a mainline backup. Scheduled maintenance, localized repair, or professional cleaning is recommended to restore full operational efficiency.
sevModEg: Field Examples: Moderate root masses obstructing less than 50% of the pipe diameter, offset joints creating a physical lip, minor "bellies" (standing water/sag), or heavy scale and grease buildup.
sevMajorDef: A severe structural failure or complete operational blockage that compromises the fundamental integrity of the sewer system. These issues pose an immediate risk of hazardous sewage backup into the structure, environmental contamination, or localized soil erosion (voids) beneath the property. Immediate professional intervention is required to restore service and prevent catastrophic property damage.
sevMajorEg: Field Examples: Fractured, cracked, or completely collapsed pipe walls; severe root blockages causing a total obstruction; broken fittings; or a missing pipe floor (channel erosion).
sevMaintDef: An operational finding where the pipeline remains structurally sound, but standard preventative servicing is required to maintain proper flow mechanics and halt accelerated deterioration. Addressing these items proactively mitigates the risk of sudden blockages and avoids costly, reactive emergency repairs.
sevMaintEg: Field Examples: Routine hydro-jetting recommended for recurring grease/sludge accumulation, chemical root treatments to prevent expansion, or professional descaling to smooth out cast iron walls.
